correctness.rationale: The all-projection symmetry condition linearly excludes forbidden great-circle Fourier modes. Harmonic projection equivariance and the primary nonzero equatorial-mode lemma leave ambient degrees 0,1,3. The resulting seven homogeneous cubic harmonics are checked exactly. Four specified rational orthonormal frames give third harmonic coefficient matrix V with exact determinant 625/6912; a checker independently obtains entries by polynomial cosine/sine expansion and by complex null frames, verifies the displayed inverse, and determines its infinity norm 164/5. Genericity follows from analytic minors on SO(3)^4. For any three planes seven unknown cubic coordinates map to no more than six observables, providing a kernel; small nonzero perturbations of the sphere preserve positive support-function curvature. The Hausdorff stability inequality follows from the exact inverse and harmonic sup bounds. The finite checker is not used to assert infinite-parameter claims.

originality.rationale: The contribution is a sharp four-view support-function tomography theorem with one explicit exact rational seven-observable inverse, generic-view sufficiency and a universal three-view ambiguity. The motivating full paper establishes the threefold exception and harmonic machinery, but not the finite-view minimum; the inspected explicit cubic records concern one-dimensional support/brightness profiles. A published continuum of Fourier-mode coefficient inequalities from accessible historical claims uses infinitely many planes and does not imply finite rank-seven injectivity. Search results are not proof of historical novelty, and older finite-band sampling is a stated priority risk.

value.rationale: The exceptional threefold planar-projection class is singled out as a natural geometric tomography problem by the motivating 2026 theorem. Its nontrivial shape freedom is exactly seven real harmonic degrees, creating a motivated minimal-data question. The solution specifies four physically interpretable calibrated planar shadows, seven exactly sufficient scalar data, an explicit rational inverse and a Lipschitz estimate, together with a sharp impossibility for any three views even near the round ball. This is not an arbitrary choice of parameters and is not simply a known scalar cubic brightness computation; it sets a self-contained minimal finite-view benchmark. It makes no claim of optimal conditioning or area-only recovery.
